rubric.criterion: Queries run correctly and return the right answers
rubric.comment: Top products and monthly trend queries are correct. The repeat-customer query counts orders instead of distinct customers.

rubric.criterion: Uses GROUP BY and JOIN appropriately
rubric.comment: Good use of INNER JOIN between orders and products. Consider LEFT JOIN to include cities with zero repeat customers.

rubric.criterion: Results are explained in plain business language
rubric.comment: Explanations restate the numbers but don't say what the business should do with them.

strengths: Clean, readable SQL with sensible aliases
Correct aggregation with SUM and GROUP BY
Good instinct to sort and limit results for the top 5
improvements: Use COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) when counting unique customers
Add one 'so what?' sentence after each result, e.g. 'Stock more of product X before festive months'
Format revenue numbers with thousand separators in the final report
